readings.title: Adorn Yourself with Majesty
readings.subtitle: Can You Humble the Proud?
readings.text: [Job 40:6] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered <dn>את</dn> Job out of the whirlwind, and said: [7] <dq>“Now gird up your loins like a man; <dn>I</dn> ask you, and you answer <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>“Would you indeed annul <dn>My</dn> right-ruling? Would you declare <dn>Me</dn> wrong so that you might be righteous?</dq> [9] <dq>“And do you have an arm like <dn>El</dn>? Or do you thunder with a voice like <dn>His</dn>?</dq> [10] <dq>“Adorn yourself, please, with excellency and splendour, And put on esteem and beauty.</dq> [11] <dq>“Scatter the rage of your wrath; And look on everyone who is proud, and humble him.</dq> [12] <dq>“Look on everyone who is proud, humble him, And tread down the wrong-doers in their place.</dq> [13] <dq>“Hide them in the dust together, Bind their faces in the hidden place.</dq> [14] <dq>“Then even <dn>I</dn> would confess to you That your own right hand saves you.</dq>

readings.title: Behemoth
readings.subtitle: The Chief of the Ways of El
readings.text: [Job 40:15] <dq>“See now Behemoth, which <dn>I</dn> made along with you; He eats grass like an ox.</dq> [16] <dq>“See now, his strength is in his loins, And his power is in the stomach muscles.</dq> [17] <dq>“He moves his tail like a cedar; The sinews of his thighs are tightly woven.</dq> [18] <dq>“His bones are tubes of bronze, His limbs like bars of iron.</dq> [19] <dq>“He is the beginning of the ways of <dn>El</dn>; <dn>His</dn> <dn>Maker</dn> brings near <dn>His</dn> sword.</dq> [20] <dq>“For the mountains yield food for him, And all the beasts of the field play there.</dq> [21] <dq>“He lies under the lotus trees, In a covert of reeds and marsh.</dq> [22] <dq>“The lotus trees cover him with their shade; The willows by the stream surround him.</dq> [23] <dq>“See, if a river rages, he is not alarmed; He feels safe, even if the Yarden gushes into his mouth,</dq> [24] <dq>“Before his eyes, shall he be caught, With snares, shall his nose be pierced?</dq>

readings.title: Leviathan
readings.subtitle: King Over All the Sons of Pride
readings.text: [Job 41:1] <dq>“Draw out Leviathan with a hook, Or snare his tongue with a line which you lower?</dq> [2] <dq>“Put a cord through his nose, Or pierce his jaw with a hook?</dq> [3] <dq>“Would he make many pleas to you? Would he speak softly to you?</dq> [4] <dq>“Would he make a covenant with you? Would you take him as a servant forever?</dq> [5] <dq>“Would you play with him as with a bird? Or leash him for your young girls?</dq> [6] <dq>“Would trading partners bargain over him? Would they divide him among the merchants?</dq> [7] <dq>“Fill his skin with harpoons? Or his head with fishing spears?</dq> [8] <dq>“Lay your hand on him; Remember the battle – never do it again!</dq> [9] <dq>“See, his expectation is deceptive; Is he cast down even at the sight of him?</dq> [10] <dq>“No one is so bold as to stir him up. Who then is able to stand against <dn>Me</dn>?</dq> [11] <dq>“Who has anticipated <dn>Me</dn>, that <dn>I</dn> should repay? All under the heavens is <dn>Mine</dn>.</dq> [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> do not keep silent concerning his limbs, Or his mighty power, or the grace of his frame.</dq> [13] <dq>“Who shall take off the surface of his garment? Who comes with his double bridle?</dq> [14] <dq>“Who shall open the doors of his face, With his terrible teeth all around?</dq> [15] <dq>“His rows of scales are his pride, Shut up as with a tight seal.</dq> [16] <dq>“One is so near to another, That no air comes between them;</dq> [17] <dq>“They are joined one to another, They stick together and are not separated.</dq> [18] <dq>“His sneezings flash light, And his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.</dq> [19] <dq>“Out of his mouth go burning torches, Sparks of fire shoot out.</dq> [20] <dq>“Smoke goes out of his nostrils, As from a boiling pot and burning rushes.</dq> [21] <dq>“His breath kindles coals, And a flame goes out of his mouth.</dq> [22] <dq>“Strength dwells in his neck, And fear leaps before him.</dq> [23] <dq>“The folds of his flesh are joined together; They are firm on him and cannot be moved.</dq> [24] <dq>“His heart is as hard as stone, Even as hard as the lower millstone.</dq> [25] <dq>“When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid; Because of breakings they are bewildered.</dq> [26] <dq>“Though the sword reaches him, it does not hold; The spear, the dart, or the javelin.</dq> [27] <dq>“He reckons iron as straw, Bronze as rotten wood.</dq> [28] <dq>“The arrow does not make him flee; Sling-stones become like stubble to him.</dq> [29] <dq>“Clubs are reckoned as straw; He laughs at the rattle of the javelin.</dq> [30] <dq>“His undersides are like sharp potsherds; He spreads pointed marks in the mire.</dq> [31] <dq>“He makes the deep boil like a pot; He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.</dq> [32] <dq>“He leaves a shining path behind him; One would think the deep to be grey-haired.</dq> [33] <dq>“On earth there is no one like him, Which is made without fear.</dq> [34] <dq>“He looks on <dn>את</dn> all that is high; He is king over all the sons of pride.”</dq>

readings.title: Job's Repentance
readings.subtitle: Now My Eye Sees You
readings.text: [Job 42:1] Then Job answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, [2] “I know that <dn>You</dn> are able to do all, And that no purpose of <dn>Yours</dn> is withheld from <dn>You</dn>. [3] “<dn>You</dn> asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ Therefore I have declared what I did not understand; Too wonderful for me, which I did not know. [4] “Please listen, and let me speak; <dn>You</dn> said, ‘<dn>I</dn> ask you, and you answer <dn>Me</dn>.’ [5] “I have heard of <dn>You</dn> by the hearing of the ear, But now my eye sees <dn>You</dn>. [6] “Therefore I despise myself, And I repent in dust and ashes.”

readings.title: Restoration and Blessing
readings.subtitle: The Latter Days of Job
readings.text: [Job 42:7] And it came to be, after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken <dn>את</dn> these words to Job, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Eliphaz the Tĕmanite, <dq>“<dn>My</dn> wrath is kindled against you and your two friends, for you have not spoken of <dn>Me</dn> what is right, as <dn>My</dn> servant Job has.</dq> [8] <dq>“And now, take seven bulls and seven rams, and go to <dn>My</dn> servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering. And let <dn>My</dn> servant Job pray for you. For <dn>I</dn> accept him, lest <dn>I</dn> deal with you according to your folly, because you have not spoken of <dn>Me</dn> what is right, as <dn>My</dn> servant Job has.”</dq> [9] So Eliphaz the Tĕmanite and Bildad the Shuḥite and Tsophar the Na‛amathite went and did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded them. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> accepted <dn>את</dn> Job. [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned <dn>את</dn> the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave Job twice as much as he had before. [11] And all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all those who had been his acquaintances before, came to him and ate food with him in his house. And they sympathized with him and comforted him for all the evil that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had brought upon him. And they each gave him one piece of silver and each a ring of gold. [12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning; for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys. [13] And he had seven sons and three daughters. [14] And he called the name of the first Yemimah, and the name of the second Qetsi‛ah, and the name of the third Qeren-Happuḵ. [15] And in all the land were found no women so fair as the daughters of Job. And their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers. [16] And after this Job lived one hundred and forty years, and saw <dn>את</dn> his children and <dn>את</dn> grandchildren for four generations. [17] So Job died, old and satisfied with days.
